title: Zone of the Enders
subtitle: A machine on a damaged colony
summary: Zone of the Enders is Konami's PlayStation 2 mecha action game, released in Japan on 1 March 2001. A military attack leaves the young Leo Stenbuck inside Jehuty, a powerful machine called an Orbital Frame. He must deliver it to friendly forces while deciding how to respond to the people still in danger around him. The adventure puts its battles in the air, allowing Jehuty to hover, rise and move between buildings. Its mechanical design gives the player a readable, agile figure amid the destruction.
body: Zone of the Enders is Konami's PlayStation 2 mecha action game, released in Japan on 1 March 2001. A military attack leaves the young Leo Stenbuck inside Jehuty, a powerful machine called an Orbital Frame. He must deliver it to friendly forces while deciding how to respond to the people still in danger around him. The adventure puts its battles in the air, allowing Jehuty to hover, rise and move between buildings. Its mechanical design gives the player a readable, agile figure amid the destruction.

Jehuty changes its attacks according to the distance from a target. Moving close brings the machine into blade range, while greater separation favours ranged fire. The player can dash around enemies and use a burst of power to break the rhythm of a fight. Because movement is not confined to the ground, approaching an opponent also means choosing a height and direction. Encounters move quickly between pursuit and contact, with the lock-on system keeping the selected enemy central while the surrounding colony slides past.

Some missions ask Leo to defend inhabited areas, making the condition of the colony part of the result. The story's civilian viewpoint gives those assignments a reason beyond destroying another formation. Noriaki Okamura directed the game, Hideo Kojima produced it, and Yoji Shinkawa designed the machines. Critics welcomed the presentation and combat but questioned the short campaign. The setting continued through other games and animation, while the direct PlayStation 2 sequel, The 2nd Runner, developed Jehuty's combat further in 2003 with a different protagonist.
